findings.passage: “These local laws fly in the face of existing law and our constitution, which I took an oath to defend – and which protects the rights of all Pennsylvanians to defend themselves and bear arms,” Burns said.

subjects: local governments making their own gun rules

findings.passage: “It is insulting to mandate that responsible, law-abiding Pennsylvanians be forced to register their firearms and pay yearly fees, just to exercise their constitutional right to own a gun,” Burns said.
findings.note: News release opposing H.B. 768, which would charge a yearly fee per registered firearm and add fingerprinting and background checks.

findings.passage: "If we want to send a clear message to criminals and those who would do others harm via gunfire, the legal system needs to enforce the laws already on the books and stop plea bargaining these types of crimes.”
findings.note: Says existing laws should be enforced and plea bargains stopped for gun crimes.

findings.passage: “Emergency declaration or not, the fundamental constitutional rights of Americans shall not be infringed,” Burns said.

findings.passage: “I seriously doubt that many, if any, gun-related crimes in Cambria County or elsewhere are committed by someone wielding a shotgun purchased at a gun show,” Burns said.

findings.passage: Burns said he sees potential for the “red flag” law to be abused – and perhaps even weaponized – by spouses, other family members and the courts.

findings.passage: “As chairman of the Second Amendment Caucus, I feel it’s important to know your rights as a law-abiding gun owner,” Burns said.
